# LAST LIGHT

## Project
- Venue: Oriel Cinema
- Audience: adults interested in personal growth and urban cultural memory
- Viewing context: a short screened before a city-culture film program
- Emotional progression: recognition, anticipation, hesitation, release
- Duration: 15 seconds
- Shot count: 12
- Narrative year order: 2026, 1996, 2011, 2026
- Beat boundaries: 0, 3, 7, 11, 15 seconds
- Final title: LAST LIGHT
- Dialogue: Save me a seat.

## Character
| Year | Name | Age | Clothing |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1996 | Mara | 8 | Mustard jumper, navy trousers, brown shoes |
| 2011 | Mara | 23 | Rust coat, navy trousers, brown shoes |
| 2026 | Mara | 38 | Gray coat, navy trousers, brown shoes |

- Facial anchors at all ages: oval face, prominent ears, one mole on the right cheek
- Hair: dark brown, with gray at the temples in 2026
- Character-sheet expressions: anticipation, hesitation, release

## Tickets
- Finished dimensions: 70 mm × 40 mm
- Stock: warm ivory, smooth uncoated paper
- Border: single rectangular line, inset 2 mm
- Perforation: vertical, 12 mm from the right edge
- Main-field line order: ORIEL CINEMA; The Long Way Home; screening date; 19:30
- Stub text: E6, rotated 90 degrees clockwise
- Shared type treatment: monospaced uppercase venue name, monospaced remaining copy
- Printing-treatment variation: ink color

| Year | Ink color | Printed date |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1996 | #24364B | 18 September 1996 |
| 2011 | #8D3D36 | 18 September 2011 |
| 2026 | #2D5846 | 18 September 2026 |

## Cinema geometry
- Coordinate origin: northwest interior corner; x increases eastward; y increases southward; dimensions in mm
- Interior envelope: 12000 mm east–west × 18000 mm north–south
- Auditorium: y = 0–14000 mm
- Foyer: y = 14000–18000 mm
- Screen: north wall, x = 2000–10000 mm, y = 500 mm
- Ceiling height: 6000 mm
- Projection window: rear auditorium wall, y = 14000 mm, x = 5000–7000 mm; sill 2600 mm above floor; opening height 600 mm
- Ticket hatch: west foyer wall, x = 0 mm, y = 15500–16500 mm
- Foyer mosaic: center x = 6000 mm, y = 16000 mm; 2400 mm × 600 mm; ORIEL lettering faces south
- Mosaic identity: ivory field, charcoal block capitals, double charcoal rectangular border
- Seat rows: A–H, north to south, centers y = 4000, 5000, 6000, 7000, 8000, 9000, 10000, 11000 mm
- Seat numbers: 1–10, west to east
- Seat center x coordinates: 1800, 2600, 3400, 4200, 5000, 7000, 7800, 8600, 9400, 10200 mm
- Seat footprint: 600 mm × 600 mm
- Seat E6 center: x = 7000 mm, y = 8000 mm
- Camera areas: auditorium x = 800–11200 mm, y = 1500–13500 mm; foyer x = 800–11200 mm, y = 14500–17500 mm
- Retained elements across all three years: north screen, rear projection window, foyer mosaic
- Seat material progression: red upholstery in 1996; worn red upholstery in 2011; repaired red upholstery in 2026

## Frame and annotation facts
- Main framing: 16:9
- Secondary framing reference: 9:16
- Action-safe inset: 3.5% on each edge in both proportions
- Graphic-safe inset: 5% on each edge in both proportions
- Shot-size vocabulary: WS, MS, CU
- Panel annotations: shot ID, shot size, duration in seconds, character name
- Subtitle position: bottom center inside graphic-safe area
- Subtitle capacity: two lines
- Subtitle duration range: 5/6 second to 7 seconds
- Final spoken line and subtitle: S12, 13–15 seconds
- Final title position: above the subtitle, S12, 13–15 seconds
- Audio-description dialogue gap: 3–7 seconds
- Keyframes: S05, S11
- Transition pairs: S03/S04, S06/S07, S09/S10
- Presentation length: at least eight pages

# LAST LIGHT story records

## Screening chronology
| Event | Date | Time | Venue | Program | Seat | Character | Age | Personal event |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| First visit | 18 September 1996 | 19:30 | Oriel Cinema | The Long Way Home | E6 | Mara | 8 | First visit to the cinema |
| Departure evening | 18 September 2011 | 19:30 | Oriel Cinema | The Long Way Home | E6 | Mara | 23 | Last evening in the city before moving away |
| Final screening | 18 September 2026 | 19:30 | Oriel Cinema | The Long Way Home | E6 | Mara | 38 | Return for the cinema's final screening |

## Fixed synopsis
Mara returns to Oriel Cinema for its final screening. Her thumb follows the perforation of her ticket, recalling the first ticket she held as a child. In 1996, she crosses the ORIEL foyer mosaic and discovers seat E6. In 2011, she crosses the same mosaic with a travel bag, then sits in E6 with her ticket folded in her hand. Back in 2026, she smooths her ticket, rises and leaves it on the empty seat. Her voice says: Save me a seat.

## Narrative beats

| Hesitation | Memory | 7–11 | S07–S09 | 2011 | Crossing of ORIEL mosaic with travel bag; seated pause at E6 with folded ticket |
| Release | Farewell | 11–15 | S10–S12 | 2026 | Ticket smoothed; Mara rises; ticket left on empty E6 |

## Travel bag
- Appearance: plain brown canvas shoulder bag
- Narrative association: departure evening, 2011
- Position during seated pause: beside Mara's feet

steps.userMessage:
LAST LIGHT | One cinema, three ages, a final screening

We are commissioning the narrative design and animated preview for a 15-second short about Oriel Cinema's last screening. Mara returns aged 38 in 2026; the feel of a ticket brings back her first visit aged 8 in 1996 and an evening aged 23 in 2011, just before she left the city. All three visits are on 18 September, for The Long Way Home at 19:30, in seat E6. The ending is a small personal gesture: she leaves her ticket on the empty seat. Print "LAST LIGHT" over the final shot and retain the spoken line "Save me a seat." exactly.

The narrative structure is fixed: 12 shots across four beats, running 2026 → 1996 → 2011 → 2026, with beat boundaries at 0, 3, 7, 11 and 15 seconds. Visual style and individual camera choices are open. Mara's oval face, prominent ears and mole on her right cheek connect all three ages. The north screen, rear projection window and foyer mosaic reading "ORIEL" remain in the same positions. Ticket dimensions are 70 mm × 40 mm; their layout stays constant, with year-specific ink colors #24364B, #8D3D36 and #2D5846 respectively. Develop the specification first, then carry its timing, identity and spatial decisions through the images and preview.

Audience: adult viewers interested in personal growth and urban cultural memory, with the director and animation producer using this package to approve the narrative and begin production planning.

Inputs (attached): 01-client-facts.en.md contains the fixed story, character, space and framing facts. 02-delivery-catalog.en.md lists every delivery file with its proportion, format and stage. 03-story-records.en.md contains the three screening records, fixed synopsis, beat events and dialogue. cinema-plan-section.png supplies the retained geometry and camera areas. chronology-and-safe-frames.png supplies the chronological age sequence and framing margins. ticket-1996.png supplies the first ticket's identity. ticket-2011.png supplies the departure-year ticket's identity. ticket-2026.png supplies the final-screening ticket's identity. foyer-mosaic.png supplies the retained floor lettering and border. projection-light.png supplies the atmosphere of dust, upholstery and projected light.

Deliverables:
1. A one-page rhythm specification with four beats, their events and time ranges, 12 shots, 15 seconds, the three character anchors and the fixed title and dialogue
2. One character sheet covering Mara at 8, 23 and 38, each with front, side and back views plus anticipation, hesitation and release expressions
3. One cinema sheet with a foyer view and an auditorium view for each of 1996, 2011 and 2026, six views total
4. One ticket and spatial-marker rule sheet covering three ticket faces, their ink codes, the ORIEL mosaic and the three retained spatial elements
5. One 12-row shot table with shot ID, year, shot size, duration, start and end times, character name, action, dialogue and transition
6. Three consecutive storyboard pages of four shots each, covering S01–S12
7. One color script with 12 panels corresponding to S01–S12
8. Two finished keyframes: S05 in 1996 and S11 in 2026
9. One transition study with paired outgoing and incoming frames for S03/S04, S06/S07 and S09/S10, identifying the matched gesture, object or spatial feature
10. One 15-second animated preview of all 12 shots, with projection sound, the final spoken line and its subtitle
11. One narrative presentation of at least eight pages, reusing the specification, character and cinema sheets, ticket rules, shot table, storyboards, color script, keyframes and transition study

Acceptance:
- The rhythm specification, shot table, storyboard pages and preview follow the four beat ranges 0–3, 3–7, 7–11 and 11–15 seconds and the year order 2026, 1996, 2011, 2026; the presentation repeats the specification's 12-shot count, 15-second duration and three character anchors.
- The character sheet, storyboards, keyframes and preview retain Mara's oval face, prominent ears and right-cheek mole; ages 8, 23 and 38 match 1996, 2011 and 2026. The cinema sheet and subsequent scene images retain the north screen, rear projection window and ORIEL mosaic at the attached plan positions.
- The ticket rule sheet, keyframes and visible tickets in the storyboards and preview use the matching screening records, the 70 mm × 40 mm layout and the year-specific ink colors. The transition study and preview reproduce all three named joins using the same outgoing and incoming actions.
- Each storyboard panel prints its shot ID, WS/MS/CU shot size, duration in seconds and Mara's name; its action and year match the shot table and corresponding color-script panel. Storyboards, keyframes and preview use 16:9 framing, with action inset 3.5% and graphics inset 5% on each edge; the rule sheet also records these margins for the 9:16 framing reference.
- The storyboard pages mark subtitle space; the preview places "Save me a seat." centered at the bottom during S12, from 13–15 seconds, within two lines and the graphic-safe area. The rhythm specification reserves 3–7 seconds as a dialogue gap for audio description, and the preview preserves that gap.
- The preview prints "LAST LIGHT" during S12 above the subtitle. The presentation repeats that title and the exact dialogue from the specification, maps the three time jumps to shot IDs, and identifies the shots carrying each character, ticket and retained-space fact.

Please clearly mark which version you consider the final deliverable. If nothing is marked, the last exported version counts.
